 From Skyfall to pricefall: Millionaire James Bond superfan slashes cost of his £2.25million 007-themed mansion
 By JOHN SIDDLE 
 Published: 19:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:46 EST, 16 November 2026 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> A Daniel Craig-lookalike who transformed his sprawling mansion into a James Bond-inspired man cave has slashed its asking price... after failing to find someone with licence to spend.
 Entrepreneur Dean Reep spent years turning his luxury six-bedroom home in Retford, Nottinghamshire, into a 007 shrine, complete with hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of memorabilia.
 However, despite going to extraordinary lengths to recreate the glamorous world of the fictional spy, Mr Reep has been forced to bring down the price of his spectacular property, aptly named Skyfall.
 The sprawling 11,000 sq ft mansion hit the market last year with a £3million asking price. But after a series of cuts in July and September, Mr Reep is now entertaining offers over £2.25million.
 Estate agents Fine & Country describe the six-bed home as a 'truly exceptional private residence'.
 The mansion is packed with rare film props, signed photographs and memorabilia spanning the entire Bond era from Sean Connery and Roger Moore to Daniel Craig .
 Among the collection is Sir Roger's gold-plated Seiko watch from Moonraker, rare Aston Martin DB5 blueprints and items from the sets of Skyfall and Quantum of Solace.
 James Bond fans have the chance to own the ultimate 007-themed house
 Dean Reep runs a company called Universal Exports Worldwide Ltd - a nod to the fictional company used as a front for MI6 in the Bond films
 A collection of supercars, including an Aston Martin, parked in the Bond fan's garage
 Estate agents Fine & Country describe the six-bed home as a 'truly exceptional private residence' 
 The Bond-mad owner also boasts an Aston Martin DBS with a 007 number plate as well as steering wheels and wing badges from some of the original movie cars
 Portrait pictures depicting scenes from the movies adorn most walls inside the 11,000 sq ft property in Retford, Nottinghamshire
 The listing states: 'One of the most impressive, if not the most impressive homes to come to the open market in recent times'
 The firm says in sales literature: 'Skyfall represents one of the most distinctive homes to come to the market in Nottinghamshire.
 'Combining architectural grandeur, bespoke craftsmanship and a design narrative inspired by the world of James Bond, this remarkable estate offers a lifestyle rarely found within a single residence.'
 Visitors are greeted by two huge stag sculptures at the electric gates, inspired by those seen outside Bond's ancestral home in the 2012 blockbuster Skyfall.
 Inside, giant portraits depicting scenes from the films adorn the walls, while metal railings around the bay windows are replicas of those seen at Bond's apartment in Spectre.
 The master suite has even featured a leather chair from Spectre, M's chair and stunt jackets from Quantum of Solace and Skyfall.
 Mr Reep, who runs a number of businesses including a technology firm, has even set up a company called Universal Exports Worldwide Ltd – a nod to the fictional company used as a front for MI6 in the Bond films.
 The 53-year-old father, who bought the property for £750,000 in 2017, was previously reported to own an Aston Martin DBS bearing a personalised 007 number plate.
 Entrepreneur Mr Reep runs a number of businesses including a technology firm
 Mr Reep bought the Nottinghamshire property for £750,000 in 2017
 Other signed memorabilia and artefacts date back to the George Lazenby, Connery and Moore eras all the way through to Daniel Craig
 The mansion contains a Bond-themed cocktail bar, games room and full-size snooker area, as well as a private gym, steam room and spa-style bathroom.
 Outside, the extravagance continues with a sweeping driveway, triple garage and a 'Wimbledon-inspired tennis court complete with adjacent pavilion'.
 The listing states: 'Skyfall is unique not simply because of its size or specification, but because of the extraordinary story behind it.
 'The property has been thoughtfully designed around the world of James Bond, with subtle references and carefully curated memorabilia creating a private celebration of one of cinema's most iconic franchises.
 'From the moment of arrival, the Bond influence is evident, with stag sculptures inspired by the gates featured in the film Skyfall and bespoke details throughout the home.
 'Within the residence is an impressive collection of Bond memorabilia spanning generations of the franchise, including rare signed artefacts, Aston Martin references, film-set pieces, production memorabilia and items connected to legendary Bond actors and films.'
